library(tidyverse)

#### **Research Question (from Scenario)**

Your task is to utilize these datasets to create county-level measures to accomplish two goals.

1.  The first is to compare county asthma ED rates with a county CES measure to assess if there appears to be a correlation. (Sadia)

2.  The second is to compare asthma ED rates with county-level summaries for specific environmental measures to determine if those specific measures may be worth further investigation. (Yijun)

#Data import

```{r message=FALSE}
# Read data and clean the variable names
ces_measure <- read_csv("https://github.com/PHW290/phw251_projectdata/raw/refs/heads/main/scenario_3/calenviroscreen_measures_2021.csv") %>% clean_names()
ces_scores_demog <- read_csv("https://github.com/PHW290/phw251_projectdata/raw/refs/heads/main/scenario_3/calenviroscreen_scores_demog_2021.csv") %>% clean_names()
chhs_asthma <- read_csv("https://github.com/PHW290/phw251_projectdata/raw/refs/heads/main/scenario_3/chhs_asthma_ed.csv") %>% clean_names()

```

### 1 Final datasets for creation of visualization

- Join all datasets together

- Calculate any remaining data elements needed for analysis

- Show code used to create joined dataset, but please do not print full data frame output (showing data structure with str() is okay)

We selected the following columns from each data and joined them together:

- ces_measure: pm2.5, drinking_water, haz_waste

- ces_scores_demog: ces_4_0_score

- chhs_asthma: age_adjusted ED visit rate, most recent year = 2020, total population

```{r}
# data cleaning for ces_measure: uniform county name & recategorize to county level
ces_measure_prep <- ces_measure %>% 
  rename(county = california_county) %>% 
  group_by(county) %>% 
  summarise(avg_pm2_5 = mean(pm2_5, na.rm = TRUE),
            avg_drinking_water = mean(drinking_water, na.rm = TRUE),
            avg_haz_waste = mean(haz_waste, na.rm = TRUE))

# data cleaning for ces_scores_demog: uniform county name & recategorize to county level
ces_scores_demog_prep <- ces_scores_demog %>% 
  mutate(county = str_remove(county, " County")) %>% 
  group_by(county) %>% 
  summarise(avg_ces_score = weighted.mean(ces_4_0_score, 
                                          w = total_population, 
                                          na.rm = TRUE))
  
# data cleaning for asthma data: used total_population & year = 2020 &
chhs_asthma_prep <- chhs_asthma %>% 
  mutate(county = str_to_title(str_trim(county))) %>% 
  filter(county != "California",
         strata == "Total population",
         year == 2020) %>% 
  select(county, age_adjusted_ed_visit_rate)

# Join 3 data sets
data_joined = left_join(x = chhs_asthma_prep,
                        y = ces_scores_demog_prep,
                        by = "county")

data_joined = left_join(x = data_joined,
                        y = ces_measure_prep,
                        by = "county")
```

### 2 Visualizations

- One print quality table as requested in scenario

- One print quality plot or chart as requested in scenario

#### 2.1 Print Quality Table (Yijun)

Research question 2: compare asthma ED rates with county-level summaries for specific environmental measures (PM 2.5; Drinking Water; and Hazardous Waste) to determine if those specific measures may be worth further investigation.

```{r}
envir_measure = c("PM 2.5", "Drinking Water", "Hazardous Waste")
correlation = c(
  cor(data_joined$age_adjusted_ed_visit_rate,
      data_joined$avg_pm2_5,
      use = "complete.obs"),
  cor(data_joined$age_adjusted_ed_visit_rate,
      data_joined$avg_drinking_water,
      use = "complete.obs"),
  cor(data_joined$age_adjusted_ed_visit_rate,
      data_joined$avg_haz_waste,
      use = "complete.obs"))

p_value = c(
  cor.test(data_joined$age_adjusted_ed_visit_rate,
           data_joined$avg_pm2_5)$p.value,
  cor.test(data_joined$age_adjusted_ed_visit_rate,
           data_joined$avg_drinking_water)$p.value,
  cor.test(data_joined$age_adjusted_ed_visit_rate,
           data_joined$avg_haz_waste)$p.value)

table1 <- tibble(envir_measure, correlation, p_value) 

kable(table1,
      col.names = c("Envirenmental Measures", "Pearson Correlation", "p-value"),
      digits = c(0,2,3),
      align = "lcc",
      caption = "Correlation between Asthma ED Visit Rates and 3 Environmental Measures in California Counties") %>% 
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE)
      
```

Interpretation: The age-adjusted asthma ED visit rate showed weak correlations with PM2.5 (r = -0.07), Drinking Water (r = 0.07), and Hazardous Waste (r = -0.18), and none of these correlations were statistically significant (all p \> 0.05). Based on this county-level analysis, there is no strong evidence of a association between asthma ED visit rates and these 3 environmental measures.
